title: Apply to get married by the NSW Registry
summary: Find out the requirements and steps to get married through the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages.
intro:
The NSW Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages offers a range of affordable wedding ceremony packages. The Registry is based in Pyrmont, Sydney and holds weddings once a month at the Old Wollongong Courthouse and at additional venues on select dates.

You do not need to contact the Registry if you plan to be married by a private celebrant, minister of religion, or registrar at a local court. You can follow the guide for getting married in NSW.

The Notice of Intended Marriage remains valid for up to 18 months.
who_can_apply: If a person under 18 wishes to marry, a court empowered to give a 'Section 12' order must give authority for the marriage.
Two persons aged under 18 years are not permitted to marry each other.
A Notice of Intended Marriage can be lodged before the 18th birthday, provided the marriage occurs after the birthday.
You can lodge a Notice of Intended Marriage while a divorce is pending, but you cannot be married until you are legally not married to anyone in Australia or any other country.
If you have already been legally married in another country, your marriage must not violate Australian law.
what_you_need: The PDF form 'Notice of Intended Marriage'.
If either person has been previously married, proof that the marriage has ended (e.g., divorce).
Any documents in a language other than English must be officially translated into English by an authorised interpreter/translation service.
If either party does not speak English fluently, someone who can interpret must be present at the marriage interview and the marriage ceremony.
Originals of your documents must be seen by the celebrant before the marriage can go ahead; photocopies are not accepted.

more_info.text: After the Notice of Intended of Marriage is lodged you must wait one month before you can be married. A Notice of Intended Marriage is valid for up to 18 months.
The Registry lodgement fee is non-refundable.
Most ceremony packages include an official certificate of marriage and a commemorative marriage certificate.

faqs.q: Do I need to contact the Registry if I plan to get married elsewhere?
faqs.a: No, you do not need to contact the Registry if you plan to be married by a private celebrant, minister of religion, or registrar at a local court.

faqs.q: How long is a Notice of Intended Marriage valid for?
faqs.a: The Notice of Intended Marriage remains valid for up to 18 months.

faqs.q: What are the minimum age requirements to get married?
faqs.a: The marriageable age is 18 years. If a person under 18 wishes to marry, a court empowered to give a 'Section 12' order must give authority for the marriage.
